purpose: Measure the tmQM (production, DFT-geometry) cohort on the same axes T57-T63 used for the CSV/ETKDG cohort, to decide whether T63's fake coordination sphere applies to the path the generated pool was actually trained on.
findings: The tmQM cohort has a REAL coordination sphere: 3.44 donors within 2.6 A per cloud (histogram {0:17,1:18,2:48,3:165,4:51,5:42,6:59}), M-L nearest distance p10 1.766 / median 2.118 / p90 2.341 A, dative 2.92 pairs per cloud.
Geometry is DFT-optimised: minimum atom-pair distance 1.127 A, 0 of 400 clouds has a pair below 1 A. Compare the CSV path, where T57 found 8,782 coincident pairs before the fix.

T63's '72% of clouds have one donor' is a CSV-path defect only. c8 -- the only run that ever produced a generated pool -- trained on tmQM, so the disconnected-SMILES failure cannot be attributed to a fake coordination sphere.
52.1% of bond labels are AROMATIC on tmQM (vs 68.4% on the CSV path); dative is 2.92 pairs/cloud vs 1.30.
This 400-cloud draw is itself metal-biased (Ru/Re/Os, zero Pt) -- see wfa113_t67_tmqm_draw.json; the coordination statistics are not sensitive to that, but the metal mix is.
honest_limits: 400 clouds, seed 0, scaffold train split. The donor count uses the builder's element set (N/O/S/P + halides), not the Wiberg BO graph.
donors_within_2.6 is a distance proxy; the bond graph's own dative count (2.92) is the label the head sees.
